gloss: to come out ahead; to gain; to benefit

definitions.gloss: to come out ahead; to gain an advantage; to benefit
definitions.explanation: To end up better off than one otherwise would — paying less, getting extra value, or gaining some advantage. The direct opposite of {損|そん}をする.

examples.japanese: まとめて{買|か}うと{得|とく}をする。
examples.english: You come out ahead if you buy in bulk.

examples.japanese: {早|はや}めに{予約|よやく}したので、{千円|せんえん}{得|とく}をした。
examples.english: I booked early, so I saved a thousand yen.

examples.japanese: {会員|かいいん}になると、{割引|わりびき}や{特典|とくてん}があって{得|とく}をすることが{多|おお}い。
examples.english: If you become a member, there are discounts and perks, so you often come out ahead.

examples.japanese: {正直|しょうじき}に{話|はな}したほうが、{結局|けっきょく}は{得|とく}をすると{思|おも}う。
examples.english: I think you come out ahead in the end by speaking honestly.

notes:
The gain is usually financial, but it can be any advantage — time, reputation, or convenience. {得|とく} also stands alone as a na-adjective ({得|とく}な{買|か}い{物|もの}, a good buy) and in the polite お{得|とく}, which is everywhere in advertising.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- ...と{得|とく}をする: you come out ahead if ...
- {得|とく}をした{気分|きぶん}: the feeling of having gotten a good deal
- {誰|だれ}も{得|とく}をしない: nobody benefits

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {損|そん}をする: to lose out — the direct opposite
- {儲|もう}かる: to make money — specifically monetary profit, usually from business
- {利益|りえき}を{得|え}る: to obtain a profit — formal, written register
